scope: F01 live selection of local index roots, retained size-on-demand outside the searchable scope

tests.nativeDesktop: node tools/search_drop_smoke.cjs --index-locations with a dedicated debug application identifier and isolated WebView2 profile

results: Using the native settings dialog, narrowed from all fixed drives to one folder. Its nested and duplicate inputs collapsed to the same root. A similarly named sibling disappeared, the previous immutable result-page handle expired, and an invalid save preserved the chosen scope.

After the first scan finished, a new nested file was indexed by the watcher. A sibling file outside the scope remained absent. Explicit folder size measurement outside the scope still returned the correct 5 bytes. Parent traversal and junction-descendant aliases returned no size and a junction-descendant root was rejected.

Moved the selected root away: the watcher status reported one unmonitored location and a fresh search returned zero fixture hits. Returning the root restored monitoring and all three fixture hits without an explicit rebuild.

After ordinary native close and restart the dialog restored the exact selected path and searches contained only the three in-scope matches. An empty explicit selection cleared the searchable index; switching to the sibling found its two files; all fixed drives could be re-enabled.

Rust coverage includes path boundaries, damaged preference recovery, old/scope-mismatched durable snapshots, retained counts and page expiration. Existing native pagination, folder size provenance, file operation receipts and restart recovery also passed.
limits: Windows 11 development machine with local fixed disks. A directory rename exercised root loss and return; physical disk unplug/replug was not tested.
The native chooser button is implemented; the automated desktop test entered real paths via the multiline editor.
The full clean Windows 10/11 installation matrix and production-provider acceptance remain open.
